title: Lead the Sheep Along

source.quote: Every small gap must be seized; every small gain must be taken. A little shade, a little light.

moral: Catch the small chances you pass by — but never let them cost you the errand.

story.title: On the Road in the Snow
story.text: Marching through the snow at night, they passed a stray sheep by the road.
story.narration: In the winter of 817, Li Su led his column through the night toward Caizhou. The snow came down hard and the road was empty — a stray sheep huddled in the snow beside it.

story.title: Taken Along in Passing
story.text: They took it along in passing, and the column never stopped.
story.narration: Li Su had the soldier beside him pick the sheep up in passing, and the column did not stop for a single step. Before dawn they reached the walls of Caizhou — the small thing was done, and the real errand was not delayed.

keyMoment.question: There is a stray sheep by the road. What do you do?

options.text: Pick it up in passing and keep the column moving
Stop and go looking for its owner
options.hint: Dawn is close; if the column stops, the errand is delayed.
A small chance you could take in passing — once it is gone, it is gone.

keyMoment.reveal: Catch the small chances you pass by — but never let them cost you the errand.

misconceptions: Leading a sheep along in passing means taking what belongs to someone else
Small chances do not matter; wait for a big one

quiz.question: Did the column stop for the sheep?
options: No — they picked it up in passing
Yes — they stopped and searched for its owner
quiz.explanation: It was something they could do in passing, so the march was not held up — the column never stopped.

quiz.question: What kind of chance does the Thirty-Six Stratagems say to take?
options: The smallest gap and the smallest gain
quiz.explanation: Every small gap must be seized and every small gain must be taken — even a small chance is worth taking.

quiz.question: On your way to school you see a lost puppy. What do you do?
options: Take it along to somewhere it can be helped, without missing school
Stay with it until its owner comes
Leave it alone — school comes first
quiz.explanation: Do your own errand first and help in passing — take it somewhere it can be helped, and you still get to school on time.
